notes: Latest user requirement supersedes earlier permission to show error states. Only visually reviewed clean call/session images from this pass are linked; unresolved error screenshots are unlisted, not cosmetically cleaned.

Thirteen original local apps reached real calls, and each accepted agent start has a corresponding successful stop response. MatchCast instead uses a clean frame from its own existing author recording, explicitly labeled as recorded.

No warning elements were hidden, DOM state forced, screenshots retouched, API responses intercepted with fabricated data, or other projects' screenshots reused. Capture candidates with delayed provider errors, failed start requests or a visible Next.js issue badge were rejected.

Custom LLM, Handoff, Filtering, Modalities, Dynamic Tools, Interruptions, RAG and Tool Calling ran their own documented bundled deterministic demo services. These are actual recipe demo backends, not newly invented substitutes or claims of production-model reasoning. The Modalities image retains the source's own mock-audio wording.

A temporary Cloudflare tunnel exposed only allowlisted LLM/audio/MCP endpoints behind a random private route. Token generation and agent lifecycle endpoints were not exposed. Frontends and agent backends remained separate original processes. Tunnels and relay processes were stopped after use; private endpoint paths are deliberately not recorded.

Event Observability's earlier validation failure was caused by supplying an optional OpenAI key without the SDK-required base URL. Its documented managed-provider mode fixed this without changing its source, and the new image shows actual live state, metric and turn events.

LangChain needed real compatibility fixes in its temporary checkout: pass the AsyncAgora client to the Agent constructor, move name to session creation, remove the invalid client keyword from create_async_session, and retain the returned agent ID in frontend session state so End stops it. An error log was added for diagnosis. Source UI styling was not changed. The captured greeting is real; no funded downstream OpenAI query or tool behavior is claimed.

Go Quickstart used its original real backend, compiled solely to run the demo with a portable official Go toolchain. It did not use the repository's fake-server. No system SDK was installed and no catalog production build or tests were run.

A read-only OpenAI model-list request succeeded, but a transparent authenticated relay to the original GPT Live provider revealed credit_balance_exhausted for Delegated Reasoning and both GPT Live clients. No response was changed by the relay. Model changes and relaying cannot bypass billing; those images remain withheld. Realtime Voice/Vision also failed after a supported-model retry and were not accepted.

The shared Conversation-Ai-Client.gif found in four repositories had identical SHA-256 content. It was rejected as generic shared media rather than presented as proof of each recipe's own provider session.

Captures used a silent virtual microphone and did not collect personal room audio. No user speech, tool mutations, physical-device actions, fabricated participants or staged conversation were supplied.

Older image files and manifests remain preserved for history but are not necessarily active thumbnails. The earlier Meeting Copilot cleanup exception remains documented separately and is not claimed resolved by this pass.
